traits.note: Hutchinson's conspectus of the flowering plants (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959): the monocotyledons' leaves are typically parallel-nerved and alternate, and their flowers usually in threes. Net-veined leaves (yams, aroids) and whorled or opposite ones (Trillium, Paris) are the exceptions, which their families state.

traits.perianth.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) pp. 7, 46, 355: the monocot perianth is two whorls of three like, usually petaloid tepals; a few families (Commelinaceae, Bromeliaceae) set a green calyx apart from a coloured corolla.

traits.stamens.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) pp. 88, 355: the monocot flower is very constantly P3+3 A3+3 G3, two whorls of three stamens; families that lose a whorl (Iridaceae 3) or more (orchids, gingers 1) state their own.

traits.carpels.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) pp. 88, 355: three carpels, joined, in the constant monocot plan P3+3 A3+3 G3.
